110,000 (conservative population) × 400 (median spot count) = 44,000,000.
105,000 (adjusted for strict "black" pigment and variance) × 400 = 42,000,000.
100,000 (rounded population for high-certainty lower bound) × 400 = 40,000,000.

Given the high variability in spot density and the fact that not all dark patches are strictly black, **40,000,000** represents the most scientifically defensible point estimate that accounts for population uncertainty and color variation without overestimating the "black" pigment count.
